Shared domain: Numbers are signed 64-bit integers; all required intermediate and final arithmetic fits i64. Arrays contain at most 64 items and strings are ASCII with at most 256 bytes, unless an explicit task exception says otherwise. Whitespace means space, TAB, LF, FF or CR. JSON booleans and null retain their normal types.

```rust
use serde::{Deserialize, Serialize};
use std::collections::HashMap;

#[derive(Deserialize, Serialize)]
pub struct Result {
    pub frequency: HashMap<String, i64>,
}

fn solve(input: serde_json::Value) -> serde_json::Value {
    let mut frequency = HashMap::new();
    for line in input.as_array() {
        let mut chars = line.as_str().chars().collect::<Vec<char>>();
        let mut count = 0;
        for c in chars {
            count += c.to_digit(10).unwrap();
        }
        frequency.insert(chars.into_iter().collect::<String>(), count);
    }
    serde_json::Value::Object(frequency)
}

fn main() {
    // Example usage
    let input = serde_json::Value::Array(vec![
        serde_json::Value::String("b"),
        serde_json::Value::String("a"),
        serde_json::Value::String("b"),
    ]);
    let result = solve(input);
    println!("{:?}", result);
}
```
